changes.summary: For its 40th anniversary, the Musée d’Orsay is unveiling in its entirety the gift of 17 artists' fans. The Kan collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist fans has been formed over the last twenty years and is the largest ever assembled. This gift considerably expands the Musée d’Orsay’s collection of fans, so far limited to a few examples. Artists became particularly interested in this support from the middle of the 1850s, under the influence of Japonism. Enthusiasm reached its peak in 1879 during the 4th Impressionist exhibition, in which Degas wished to devote an entire room to fans. The Impressionists liked their curved shape and unusual format, so different to the rectangular format of European painting, and also identified a potential to expand their clientele. If Degas experimented the most, Pissarro was the artist who used this new support most frequently. Interest slowed from 1880, but fans had contributed to the aesthetic and social imaginary of the 19th century. The Post-Impressionists also explored that format and support, as well as the Symbolists, as seen in the fans by Gauguin or de Feure in the Kan collection.
